subjective.unit: Chief Complaint: Irritable Bowel Syndrome (IBS) symptoms with abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting.
subjective.citation_text: Patient: I'm 32 years old, and I'm a female. I'm here because my IBS symptoms have been flaring up again, with abdominal pain, nausea, and some vomiting. It's been worse since I've been eating out more often, especially on weekends. Doctor: Could you describe the nature and location of your abdominal pain, as well as the frequency and characteristics of your nausea and vomiting? Patient: The abdominal pain is a cramping and sharp pain, mostly in my lower belly, and it comes and goes. The nausea happens more when I eat out, especially after spicy or fatty foods, and I've been vomiting occasionally, but not too often. It's been worse since I started going to Friday nights and Saturday nights out. Doctor: Have you had any prior episodes of IBS flare-ups, and if so, what was the pattern or triggers for those episodes? Additionally, have you been diagnosed with any other gastrointestinal conditions or allergies in the past? Patient: I've had IBS flare-ups before, especially around the same time last year when I was seen in August 2019. The triggers seem to be similar—eating out, spicy or fatty foods, and drinking alcohol, especially on weekends. I don't recall having any other gastrointestinal conditions or allergies, but I was prescribed Reglan before, which I used as needed for nausea. Doctor: Could you share any details about your family history of gastrointestinal disorders, as well as any physical symptoms you've noticed recently, such as abdominal tenderness, bowel sounds, or signs of dehydration? Patient: I don't have any family history of gastrointestinal disorders that I'm aware of. Recently, I haven't had any tenderness in my abdomen, and my bowel sounds seem normal. I haven't noticed any signs of dehydration, but I have been drinking more water instead of sodas, which I think has helped a little. Doctor: Have you had any recent stool tests, blood tests, or imaging studies to evaluate your current symptoms? Patient: No, I haven't had
